input: Map out a realistic clutter-free capsule wardrobe

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this covers the full wardrobe or just one category (e.g. workwear, casual) changes how many pieces to plan for and what to include.
Gender expression, body type, and personal identity heavily influence which silhouettes, fits, and garment types belong in the capsule.
A person's daily lifestyle — office job, outdoor work, stay-at-home — dictates which occasions the wardrobe must serve and in what proportions.
Budget determines whether the plan involves buying new pieces, working only with what they own, or a mix of both.
Aesthetic direction (minimalist, classic, streetwear, etc.) and color palette shape which specific items are chosen and how well pieces mix and match.
Knowing the target number of items or the feeling of 'done' tells us when the capsule is complete and prevents over-collecting.
Understanding the starting point — whether they are building from scratch or editing an existing wardrobe — determines whether the first action is auditing or shopping.

gold.taskTitle: Map Out a Realistic Clutter-Free Capsule Wardrobe
gold.taskDescription: Plan a focused, intentional capsule wardrobe by identifying the right pieces, removing excess, and building a cohesive system that fits the user's real life.

questions.title: Which areas of your wardrobe does this cover?
questions.description: Clarify whether this capsule is meant to cover the user's entire wardrobe or a specific segment such as workwear, casual everyday, travel, or seasonal clothing.

questions.title: How would you describe your gender expression and style identity?
questions.description: Understand the user's gender expression and self-presentation preferences so the capsule reflects the right silhouettes, fits, and garment types for them.

questions.title: What does a typical week of your life actually look like?
questions.description: Identify the real occasions the wardrobe must serve — office, remote work, social outings, outdoor activities — and in what proportion, so pieces are practical.

questions.title: Are you open to buying new pieces, or working with what you own?
questions.description: Determine whether budget and intent allow for new purchases, or whether the plan should focus on curating and removing from the existing wardrobe only.

questions.title: What aesthetic or color palette feels most like you?
questions.description: Pin down the user's preferred visual style (e.g. neutral minimalist, earthy tones, bold classics) so pieces are cohesive and truly mix-and-match.

questions.title: How many total items are you aiming to keep?
questions.description: Establish a target item count or a guiding principle (e.g. 30 pieces, one drawer, one rail) so the plan has a clear finish line.

questions.title: Are you starting from scratch or editing an existing wardrobe?
questions.description: Find out whether the user has a wardrobe to audit and pare down, or whether they are building the capsule from a blank slate, as this determines the very first action.
